title: Inequalities
description: Learn to solve and graph inequalities with practical applications

definition.title: What is an Inequality?
definition.intro: An inequality shows the relationship between two values when they are different. Unlike equations that use '=', inequalities use symbols like >, <, ≥, and ≤.

inequality.title: 📈 Inequality
inequality.meaning: x can be any value greater than 5

solving.title: 📝 Solving Inequalities
solving.text: Inequalities are solved like equations, with one important exception:
solving.rule1: Add or subtract the same number from both sides - inequality sign stays the same
solving.rule2: Multiply or divide by a positive number - inequality sign stays the same

flip.title: The Flip Rule
flip.text: When you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, you must flip the inequality sign!

numberline.title: 📍 Graphing on a Number Line
numberline.text: Visual representation helps understand the solution set:
numberline.open: Open circle: value not included (> or <)

table.gtGraph: Arrow to the right, open circle
table.ltGraph: Arrow to the left, open circle
table.gteGraph: Arrow to the right, closed circle
table.lteGraph: Arrow to the left, closed circle

example1.title: Example 1: Simple Inequality
example1.solutionText: x can be any number greater than 5

example2.title: Example 2: Two-Step Inequality
example2.step3Text: Divide both sides by 3 (positive number, sign stays same)
example2.solutionText: x can be 5 or any number less than 5

example3.title: Example 3: Negative Coefficient (Flip the Sign!)
example3.step2Text: Divide both sides by -4 and FLIP the inequality sign
example3.note: ⚠️ Remember: When dividing by a negative, flip the sign!
example3.solutionText: x can be any number less than -5

example4.title: Example 4: Compound Inequality
example4.solutionText: x is between -2 and 4, including 4 but not -2

realWorld.title: Real World Applications
realWorld.intro: Inequalities are everywhere in daily life when we deal with limits, ranges, and constraints!

app1.title: 💰 Budget Constraints
app1.description: When shopping with a budget, you need to stay under a spending limit.
app1.example: You have $100. You buy a $25 shirt and want to buy movie tickets for $3 each. How many tickets can you buy?
app1.answer: You can buy up to 25 tickets.

app2.title: 🌡️ Temperature Ranges
app2.description: Comfortable room temperature is often described as a range, not a single value.
app2.example: A comfortable room temperature is between 65°F and 75°F.
app2.meaning: The temperature should be at least 65° but no more than 75°.

app3.title: 🚗 Speed Limits
app3.description: Speed limits are inequalities that tell us the maximum safe speed.
app3.example: A highway has a speed limit of 65 mph.
app3.meaning: You must drive at a speed less than or equal to 65 mph to stay legal.

tip1.title: ⚠️ Don't Forget to Flip!
tip1.text: The most common mistake is forgetting to flip the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number. Always check the sign of the number you're using!

tip2.title: ✅ Test Your Solution
tip2.text: Pick a number from your solution set and substitute it back into the original inequality to verify it works. This helps catch errors!

tip3.title: 📊 Visualize with a Number Line
tip3.text: Drawing a number line helps you see the solution set clearly. Use open circles for < and >, closed circles for ≤ and ≥.

tip4.title: 🎯 Read Carefully
tip4.text: Pay attention to whether the inequality includes 'or equal to' (≤ or ≥) versus strict inequality (< or >). This determines if the boundary value is included in the solution.

conclusion.title: Summary
conclusion.summary: Great work! You've learned how to solve inequalities, one of the most practical math skills for real-world situations.
conclusion.point1: Inequalities show relationships between values using >, <, ≥, and ≤
conclusion.point2: Solve inequalities like equations, but flip the sign when multiplying/dividing by negatives
conclusion.point3: Graph solutions on number lines using open or closed circles
conclusion.point4: Inequalities appear everywhere: budgets, temperature ranges, speed limits, and more
conclusion.next: Next up: Coordinate Plane & Graphing - plotting points and visualizing equations!
